안녕하다.gloss: to be well, to be at peace

meanings.en: to be well, to be at peace
meanings.note: Mainly used in greetings like '안녕하세요'.

examples.trans: Hello? (Are you well?)
I hope everyone is well.

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.

meanings.note: Often used directly without a locative particle to mean 'here'.

examples.trans: Please sit here.
Here is our office.
Please give me some water.
Please wait just a moment.

meanings.note: Contraction of 조금
Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 안녕하세요, 저 신디인데 여기 좀 넣어주세요.
examples.trans: Hello, I am Cindy—please put these away here for me.
This expression comes from 'please put in for me'.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.note: Hangul spelling of the English abbreviation PD, widely used in Korean broadcasting.

examples.trans: Who is the PD in charge of the new program?

examples.text: 그녀는 예능 피디가 되기 위해 시험을 준비했다.
examples.trans: She prepared for the exam to become a variety PD.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.trans: Me? You remember Music Bank producer Tak Ye-jin, right?
This expression comes from 'you remember, right?'.

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization, surprise, or hesitation.

examples.trans: Ah, yes.
Oh, I see!

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 아, 화장을 안 하셔서 몰라봤어요, 죄송해요.
examples.trans: Oh, you were not wearing makeup, so I did not recognize you—I am sorry.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 아, 화장을 안 하셔서 몰라봤어요, 죄송해요.
examples.trans: Oh, you were not wearing makeup, so I did not recognize you—I am sorry.
This expression comes from 'failed to recognize'.

meanings.note: Respectful, polite adjective used to apologize in workplaces and to strangers. Formal 죄송합니다 is the standard workplace apology. RR: joesonghada.

examples.trans: I am very sorry for being late.
I am sorry for the inconvenience.

meanings.note: Humble 1st person plural pronoun used when speaking to superiors or in formal settings.

examples.trans: We will prepare first.
Welcome to our company.

meanings.note: The present day; often used adverbially without a particle.

examples.trans: The weather is nice today.
What day of the week is it today?
We have a team dinner today.
Where is the company dinner?

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: first, before others, ahead of time
meanings.note: Indicates priority in order or time.

examples.trans: It's late, so I'll head in first.
Who arrived first?
I want to went inside right now.
How about trying to went inside together tomorrow?

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 아 재수 없어, 진짜 너무 완전 재수 없어!
examples.trans: Ugh, how obnoxious—seriously, totally obnoxious!
Here the word for 'luck, vibe' is key.

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, to not be present

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken intensifier; can also function as a noun meaning 'the real thing'.

examples.trans: I'm really busy today.
Is that really delicious?

meanings.note: Used colloquially for positive or negative emphasis.
Original sense of exceeding a limit.

examples.trans: The weather is so nice today.

examples.text: 그냥 내버려 둬, 쟤 완전 취했어.
examples.trans: Just leave him alone, he is completely wasted.

meanings.note: Spontaneous exclamation of mild surprise or puzzlement when noticing something unexpected. RR: eo.

examples.trans: Huh? Where is my phone?

meanings.note: Colloquial spoken form of 너희네; used among close friends or to juniors.
